title: Beatrix and the Salt
premise: August Winterbourne owes the Salt Guild eleven years of service for a debt inherited from a mother they barely knew, keeping ledgers that record trades in impossible things: borrowed luck, second chances, years of life. When prayers to the old gods start being answered again, August discovers the gods are answering because someone beneath the mountain has been feeding them stolen souls — including the soul their mother sold before August was born. To reclaim it, August must betray the guild that owns their debt, ally with a disgraced priestess and a god who has forgotten its own name, and descend into the court beneath the mountain. In the end, August learns their mother sold her soul to buy August's freedom from the guild, and they must choose between keeping that freedom and giving it back — choosing, finally, a third path: rewriting the ledger itself, at the cost of the guild's power and their own name in the book of the living.
about_author: Quentin Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the correspondence of obscure religious orders before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, debt, and the terrible arithmetic of love, and live somewhere with very long winters.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: August's POV. We meet the Salt Guild's counting house: August balances entries for traded luck, sold shadows, and a widow's purchased grief. A routine audit turns strange when an entry appears in a hand August doesn't know — their mother's, dead twenty years. Beat: unease beneath routine, the first crack in August's orderly world.

chapters.title: Salt on the Tongue
chapters.summary: August's POV. August reports the anomaly to Guildmaster Corvane, who burns the page and warns August that curiosity is a debt with interest. That night, August dreams of a mountain breathing. Beat: the guild's menace revealed; August's loyalty tested for the first time.

chapters.title: The Prayers That Answered Back
chapters.summary: Ysolde's POV. A disgraced priestess of the old gods notices her dead god's shrine is warm again — someone is answering prayers in her city, and the answers cost the pray-ers something vital. She follows a answered prayer to the Salt Guild's door. Beat: dread and fierce hope entwined.

chapters.title: Terms of Service
chapters.summary: August's POV. Ysolde confronts August in the counting house, demanding to know what the guild is trading. August denies everything, but that evening cross-references the ledgers and finds eleven entries of souls sold 'to the court beneath the mountain' — including B. Winterbourne. Beat: denial collapsing into complicity.

chapters.title: The Debt Inherited
chapters.summary: August's POV. August reads their mother's contract: eleven years of service for a debt of one soul. They realize their entire life has been collateral. Corvane, watching, offers a promotion — silence in exchange for advancement. Beat: the vertigo of a life built on a lie.

chapters.title: A God With No Name
chapters.summary: Ysolde's POV. Ysolde and August find a god living as a beggar by the salt docks — an old god who sold its name to the guild and remembers nothing but its hunger. Ysolde recognizes its silence as the same silence that followed her god's death. Beat: grief meeting strange tenderness.

chapters.title: What the Widow Bought
chapters.summary: August's POV. August traces a soul-trade to a client: a widow who bought back her husband's last words, and received instead a voice that isn't his. The souls are being mishandled — or eaten. Beat: horror; the stakes become human and immediate.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Begins
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Snow falls in midsummer. The old gods' answering prayers are drawing heat from the world itself; the court beneath the mountain is feeding, and winter is its digestion. The city panics; the guild profits. Beat: the world tilts; private stakes become apocalyptic.

chapters.title: Breaking Contract
chapters.summary: August's POV. August decides to steal the ledger's master copy and runs. Corvane catches them at the gate — but instead of punishment, invokes a clause: August's debt transfers to whoever holds their soul-contract, and the court beneath the mountain holds their mother's. Beat: betrayal inverted; the trap becomes a map.

chapters.title: The Priestess's Confession
chapters.summary: Ysolde's POV. Ysolde admits she once served the court's priest caste and fled when asked to feed a child to the mountain. Her god died of shame. August must decide whether to trust someone whose loyalty already failed once. Beat: vulnerability; loyalty vs. truth sharpened.

chapters.title: The Salt Road Down
chapters.summary: August's POV. The three descend the old salt road into the mountain, guided by the nameless god's hunger. The world above grows colder with every mile. August keeps a ledger of what they're each willing to lose. Beat: commitment; quiet dread and camaraderie.

chapters.title: Toll
chapters.summary: Ysolde's POV. At the first gate, a toll is demanded: a memory each. August pays a memory of their mother; the god pays a memory of its name and comes out weeping without knowing why. Beat: sacrifice establishing the price of everything ahead.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: August's POV. They reach the court: a mirrored hall where the old gods' stolen souls are kept as lamps. The Court's Regent — something wearing August's mother's face — greets them courteously. Beat: uncanny horror; the personal made monstrous.

chapters.title: The Mother's Ledger
chapters.summary: August's POV. The Regent shows August the truth: their mother sold her soul to buy August out of the guild's contract — the debt August has served was a forgery Corvane kept alive. August's loyalty to the guild was loyalty to a lie. Beat: devastating revelation; grief and rage.

chapters.title: What Ysolde Owes
chapters.summary: Ysolde's POV. The court offers Ysolde her god's soul-lamp in exchange for August and the nameless god. She nearly accepts. The nameless god, recognizing her, gives her back a memory she paid at the toll — her god's forgiveness. Beat: temptation and grace; love against duty.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Souls
chapters.summary: August's POV. August negotiates with the Regent in the only language the court respects: ledger law. They discover a flaw — a soul sold under false contract can be reclaimed by the true debtor. But the true debtor is their mother's ghost, and ghosts cannot sign. Beat: intellectual climax; hope with a knife's edge.

chapters.title: Corvane Descends
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV (first guild view inside the court). Corvane arrives to collect August, revealing he has served the court for decades, feeding it souls to keep the guild's monopoly on the miraculous. He offers August partnership in the new winter. Beat: the antagonist's logic laid bare; the banality of evil.

chapters.title: The Signing
chapters.summary: August's POV. Climax. August forges their mother's hand — the one hand they've inherited — and signs the reclamation. The court's lamps go out one by one as stolen souls return to the world. The Regent unravels; Corvane is claimed by his own creditors. Beat: triumph at terrible cost — the nameless god burns itself as witness.

chapters.title: Winter Breaking
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The mountain exhales; the long winter breaks. Ysolde carries the nameless god's ashes up the salt road, and at the summit the god remembers its name at last and goes out like a satisfied lamp. Beat: elegy and release.

chapters.title: Audit
chapters.summary: August's POV. August returns to the guild and, as the only living signatory of the master ledger, dissolves it — freeing every debtor, including themselves. Corvane's empire of paper burns. Beat: justice as bookkeeping; August reclaiming their own story.

chapters.title: The Debt of Living
chapters.summary: August and Ysolde's shared POV. August visits their mother's grave with the reclaimed soul, which chooses to scatter rather than return — a gift, not a debt. Ysolde and August, both freed and unmoored, choose each other without contract. Beat: love against duty resolved into love without ledger.

chapters.title: Beatrix and the Salt
chapters.summary: Epilogue, August's POV. August learns their mother's name was Beatrix, and writes it — for the first time — in a book of their own making, not the guild's. Snow falls gently, ordinary snow. Beat: quiet closure; inheritance transformed from debt into memory, and memory into story.
